source_text: Non enim soli Ioseph, sed et Dei genitrici Mariae testimonium perhibens Lucas, in divinis Evangeliis, ad ipsam David familiam atque cognationem respiciens, enarrat ac dicit: Ascendit autem et Ioseph a Galilaea in civitatem Iudaeae, quae vocatur Bethleem, ut profiteretur cum Maria desponsata sibi uxore, praegnante: eo quod essent ipsi e domo et familia David. Factum est autem, cum essent ipsi ibi, impleti sunt dies ut pareret ipsa, et peperit filium suum primogenitum omnis creaturae: et pannis eum involuit, et reclinavit ipsum in praesepio, quia non erat eis locus in diversorio.
thought_title: Joseph and pregnant Mary register at Bethlehem and she gives birth
orientation: The homilist narrator cites Luke's Gospel to place Joseph and Mary of David's house at Bethlehem for the birth.
pass_a_gloss: For not to Joseph alone, but also bearing witness to Mary the bearer of God, Luke, in the divine Gospels, looking to the very house and kinship of David, relates and says: And Joseph also went up from Galilee into the city of Judea, which is called Bethlehem, in order that he might be registered together with Mary his betrothed wife, being pregnant: because they themselves were from the house and family of David. And it happened, when they themselves were there, the days were fulfilled that she herself should bear, and she bore her son the firstborn of all creation: and she wrapped him in cloths, and she laid him down in a manger, because there was not for them a place in the inn.

lemmas.gloss: be registered / enrolled here for census

choices.english: to Mary the bearer of God
choices.why: keeps genitive Dei doing the begetting and dative witness force, not smoothing to a title

choices.english: in order that he might be registered
choices.why: purpose subjunctive with no census noun in Latin, so no added census

choices.english: her son the firstborn of all creation
choices.why: keeps accusative apposition and full genitive phrase exactly as added to Luke wording

choices.english: in a manger / in the inn
choices.why: keeps distinct concrete nouns and the negation as cause, not generalizing to stable

quoted source words: primogenitum omnis creaturae

pass_b_english: For Luke bears witness in the divine Gospels not to Joseph alone but also to Mary the bearer of God. Looking back to the very house and lineage of David, he relates the story and says:

"Joseph went up from Galilee to a city of Judea called Bethlehem, in order that he might be registered with Mary, his betrothed wife, who was pregnant, since they themselves were of the house and family of David (Luke 2:4-5). And it happened that while they were there, the days were fulfilled for her to give birth, and she bore her son the firstborn of all creation (Colossians 1:15). She wrapped him in cloths and laid him in a manger, because there was no place for them in the inn (Luke 2:6-7)."
